newsitem.title: USA: NSC sees H2 growth in industries it serves.
newsitem.headline: NSC sees H2 growth in industries it serves.

text.p: Norfolk Southern Corp said Wednesday most of its industry groups, including chemicals and merchandise carried by its intermodal business, are on track for growth in the second half.

"For the remainder of the year, we believe the economy will continue to grow, and we expect to follow above that trend," said L.I. Prillaman, executive vice president of marketing for the rail and trucking services company.
"Again, most of our industry groups are on track for more year-over-year growth in the second half."
Prillaman released the projections during a presentation of the company's second quarter earnings in New York.
The company expects moderate growth gains continuing for its traffic in export coal and coke coal, the coal used by the steel industry.
Coal traffic, including domestic and export coal, generally makes up about a third of the rail division's operating revenues.
Agriculture traffic, the railroad's next-largest commodity, should approach year-ago levels as the company enters the second half, the company said.
In 1996, Norfolk Southern reported $393 million in agriculture traffic out of its $4.1 billion in total operating revenues in the rail division.
The railroad said it expects minimal growth for automotive traffic because of slower sales for passenger vehicles and continued shortages of bi-level rail cars through the third quarter.
It added, however, that in the second quarter it will acquire 326 new bi-level cars used to transport automobiles.

On Wednesday Norfolk Southern reported second quarter earnings of $1.52 a share, including $0.09 a share in costs for the acquisition of Conrail Corp, on transportation operating revenues of $1.304 billion. In 1996's Q2 Norfolk Southern reported earnings of $1.57 a share on transportation operating revenues of $1.278 billion.
